record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Poisson statistics for arithmetic quantum chaos
record.original_question: For arithmetic negatively curved surfaces, or analogous systems such as the quantum cat map, can one give a full rigorous proof that the two-point correlation function of the high-energy quantum spectrum converges to the correlation function of Poisson-distributed points rather than to random matrix statistics? The issue is to control the additional periodic-orbit correlations caused by large degeneracies of the length spectrum.

evidence.quote: In the case of arithmetic surfaces (or the quantum cat map), the orbit lengths are highly degenerate (they are simple functions of integer numbers), so many more pairs of orbits are correlated than in the generic case.
The above approach implies that the 2-point function converges to that of Poisson-distributed points, quite different from RMT [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider an arithmetic negatively curved surface $X = \Gamma \backslash \mathbb{H}$ (for instance $\Gamma$ a congruence subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or a unit group of an indefinite quaternion order), and let $\{E_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ denote the eigenvalues of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, ordered with multiplicity. Let $N(E)=\#\{n: E_n\le E\}$ be the eigenvalue counting function, and define the unfolded eigenvalues $x_n = N(E_n)$, which have unit mean spacing. The pair correlation function of the unfolded spectrum is, for a test function $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$,
$$ R_2(f,E) = \frac{1}{N(E)} \sum_{\substack{m,n\le N(E)\\ m\neq n}} f(x_m - x_n). $$

An analogous setup applies to the quantum cat map: for $A\in \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ hyperbolic, let $U_N(A)$ be its quantization on the $N$-dimensional Hilbert space of states on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$, with eigenphases $\{\theta_j(N)\}_{j=1}^N$, unfolded to unit mean spacing.

Problem. Prove rigorously that, in the high-energy (resp. large-$N$) limit, the pair correlation function $R_2$ converges to the Poisson pair correlation, i.e. for every $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$,
$$ \lim_{E\to\infty} R_2(f,E) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x)\,dx. $$
Equivalently, show that the contribution to $R_2$ coming from correlations among periodic orbits whose lengths are highly degenerate (since closed-geodesic lengths on arithmetic surfaces, and periods of the cat map, are simple functions of integers, producing exponentially large multiplicities in the length spectrum) can be controlled and yields the Poisson, rather than random-matrix, two-point statistics.
artifact.status_search_result: No rigorous proof of convergence of the pair correlation to the Poisson form for the Laplace spectrum on arithmetic hyperbolic surfaces or for eigenphases of quantum cat maps appears to be available. Numerical confirmation and heuristic (periodic orbit) derivations exist, but controlling the periodic-orbit correlations arising from the large degeneracies of the length spectrum remains an unresolved obstacle in the literature on arithmetic quantum chaos.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical Measures for Higher-Dimensional Quantum Cat Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Studies semiclassical measures and arithmetic eigenfunctions of cat maps; addresses QUE-type questions but not Poisson pair correlation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on arithmetic cat maps focuses on QUE/eigenfunction localization, not on a proof of Poisson pair correlation.

status_evidence.title: On Quantum Ergodicity for Higher Dimensional Cat Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes density-one equidistribution of eigenfunctions for higher-dimensional cat maps; spectral statistics of eigenphases not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Eigenphase pair-correlation statistics for arithmetic cat maps remain without rigorous proof.
